definition: The task of converting images of typed, handwritten, or printed text into machine-readable text.
details: OCR is a foundational technology for digitizing documents and is increasingly integrated into multimodal LLM pipelines that need to extract text from scanned documents, screenshots, or photos.

explainer.lead: Optical character recognition converts images of typed, handwritten or printed text into machine-readable text. It is foundational for digitizing documents and now feeds text extraction into multimodal LLM pipelines.

tiers.eli5: It looks at a picture of words and types out those words so a computer can read them.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run OCR over scans, screenshots and photos to produce text for search, indexing or downstream models. A pitfall is assuming clean output from poor images, since the task depends on the quality of the input image.
tiers.paperLevel: The task is converting images of typed, handwritten or printed text into machine-readable text; it covers printed, typed and handwritten input.

explainer.example: A photo of a receipt is passed through OCR to produce machine-readable text listing the purchased items.
